title: Artificial intelligence in immune checkpoint inhibitor research: A bibliometric analysis of the landscape

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Artificial intelligence in immune checkpoint inhibitor research: A bibliometric analysis of the landscape》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · s0001-p4】Therefore, this study presents a comprehensive bibliometric and visual knowledge-mapping analysis of global research on AI and ICIs. By evaluating publication trends, collaboration networks, influential authors and institutions, research hotspots, and emerging frontiers, we aim to provide an updated overview of the field, identify current knowledge gaps, and highlight future directions for integrating AI into precision immunotherapy.

【Introduction · s0001-p1】Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) significantly improve patient prognoses by activating the immune system.1–3 However, their efficacy varies widely, while they may induce immune-related adverse events (irAEs), underscoring the critical need for precise dosing studies.4–9 Traditional immune biomarker detection methods are costly, and their accuracy has been questioned.10 Meanwhile, these methods struggle to capture the heterogeneity and dynamic changes within the tumor microenvironment (TME).10–12 Recently, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative tool to address these challenges.13–18 By integrating multi-omics data, spatial genomics analysis, and clinical outcomes, AI is increasingly unraveling the complex interplay between immune checkpoint inhibitor dosage, therapeutic efficacy, and toxicity.19–23

【Optimizing ICIs treatment strategies and clinical trial design · s0004-s2002-p1】AI facilitates the design of personalized immunotherapy plans by integrating multi-omics and clinical data to predict which patients are most likely to benefit from specific ICIs regimens. The concept of the “cancer-immune set point” provides a framework for understanding the determinants of response, and AI models can incorporate this to stratify patients.58 Landmark clinical trials have established the efficacy of anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agents in various settings,59–66 and AI can leverage these real-world data to refine treatment selection. For instance, integrative molecular and clinical modeling has been applied to predict outcomes to PD-1 blockade in melanoma,67 and pan-tumor genomic biomarkers have been developed to guide therapy.68 Explainable AI techniques can validate these models, ensuring scientific credibility and streamlining clinical trial design by identifying promising patient subgroups and combination strategies.

【Conclusion · s0006-p1】In conclusion, this bibliometric analysis reveals a rapid and sustained expansion of AI-related ICI research over the past decade, with China and the USA emerging as the leading contributors. While the field exhibits robust quantitative growth, meaningful clinical translation remains an ongoing endeavor that will require rigorous model validation, interpretable AI architectures, and equitable data representation. Future efforts should prioritize bridging the gap between computational findings and bedside application, ensuring that AI-driven innovations ultimately translate into measurable improvements in patient outcomes.
